title: Disagreement of a sign-dependent coordinate choice
statement: Let $x$ be uniformly distributed on the three-dimensional sign cube, let $i$ be one of its three coordinates, and let $j$ assign to each sign one of the three coordinates, always different from $i$. Then the probability that $x_i$ differs from the sign at coordinate $j(x_i)$ is $1/2$.
hypotheses_covered: A map from signs to coordinates
For every sign, the chosen coordinate differs from $i$
